claims.text: A machine-learning framework using local-disorder descriptors can reliably identify single-phase high-entropy alloys with ultra-low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed framework will be more accurate than conventional DFT and empirical methods.
The proposed framework will be faster than conventional DFT and empirical methods.
The target material class consists of well-mixed, single-phase alloys containing at least four principal elements.
FeCoCrMnNi is a representative well-mixed single-phase high-entropy alloy.
FeCoCrMnNi has force-constant fluctuations of about 20%, comparable to those calculated for related binary and ternary alloys.
A model trained on binary and ternary alloy data can be extended to screen high-entropy-alloy compositions.
Mass, atomic-size, and electronegativity differences are descriptors of local chemical disorder relevant to phonon transport.
Differences in constituent atomic characteristics produce local chemical and force-constant fluctuations.
Force-constant fluctuations enhance acoustic-phonon attenuation in high-entropy alloys.
Severe lattice distortion in high-entropy materials strongly scatters heat-carrying phonons and lowers lattice thermal conductivity.
Local disorder reduces phonon lifetimes.
Correlating atomic disorder descriptors with phonon-scattering mechanisms is sufficient for the model to predict suppressed lattice thermal conductivity.
The method will identify compositions whose lattice thermal conductivity is at least 20–30% lower than values predicted by conventional DFT or empirical rules.
The method's predictions will closely match experimentally measured lattice thermal conductivity.
Current DFT and empirical models are computationally expensive and only moderately accurate for HEA lattice thermal conductivity.
The predictive approach is applicable only to single-phase, homogeneously mixed high-entropy alloys at temperatures up to about 500 K.
Prediction accuracy will degrade in multiphase, segregated, clustered, or ordered systems whose local environments differ from the training data.
Experimental lattice thermal conductivities more than 20–30% above model predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the predicted correlation between disorder descriptors and phonon-scattering rates would falsify the proposed mechanism.
